item.title: Claim Hygiene Is Part of Website QA
item.description: High-trust websites need more than polished design. Every public claim should be defensible, crawlable, and aligned with the facts the site can prove.

item.title: Structured Data Needs Verified Facts, Not Guesses
item.description: Structured data only helps when the facts are verified. Before adding schema, confirm domains, locations, social profiles, service pages, and form behavior.

item.title: We Ran a Real GEO Audit. The Score Was 56/100. Here's What That Means.
item.description: A real Generative Engine Optimization audit across four dimensions — technical, citability, schema, and brand. Here's what the scores actually revealed and what to do about them.

item.title: Why JSON-LD Schema Is the Most Overlooked Pre-Launch Task
item.description: Most websites launch without structured data. In 2026, that's a real cost — AI search tools depend on JSON-LD to understand who you are, what you do, and why you matter.

item.title: Why Local Service Businesses Score Well on Technical SEO but Fail AI Citability
item.description: Local service businesses often have solid technical SEO — HTTPS, schema, sitemap, fast load times. But when it comes to AI citability, they're invisible. Here's the structural reason why.

item.title: Your Social Links Need to Live in Two Places (And Most Sites Only Have One)
item.description: Adding social profiles to your website footer isn't enough for GEO. Learn why your Instagram and TikTok links also need to be in your JSON-LD schema's sameAs array — and why both sides working together is what AI actually reads.

item.title: From 35 to 93: What Actually Moves Structured Data Scores for Local Businesses
item.description: Most local businesses have one schema type and call it done. Here's what it looks like to go from a skeleton structured data setup to a complete machine-readable identity layer — and why 58 points of improvement matters for AI visibility.

item.title: What a 4-Dimensional AI Visibility Audit Actually Looks Like
item.description: Most GEO audits are a checklist. A real audit measures four distinct dimensions — and which one is weakest tells you more about a site than the total score does.
